Description: The oldest complete New Testament in existence, written in Greek on parchment in the fourth century, found by Constantin von Tischendorf at St. Catherine's Monastery — some leaves in a basket awaiting burning, the rest obtained in 1859. It contains the whole New Testament and much of the Greek Old Testament, with the books in an ancient order.
BiblicalSignificance: Every modern Bible is translated from manuscripts like this one. Sinaiticus lets scholars check our New Testaments against a copy made within three centuries of the apostles — and find them remarkably faithful. The word that was first preached in houses and marketplaces was already being guarded, copied, and bound as a book.
Interpretations: Scholars agree Sinaiticus is a genuine fourth-century Bible; debate concerns its place of production (Caesarea is often suggested) and the history of its leaves.
